niche: a Midwestern mutual auto insurer setting its private passenger bodily injury loss reserve at the 2026 year-end close on paid losses and claimant counts, two and a half years after a claims-platform cutover slowed the settlement of the represented claims that carry most of the dollars
answer: Carry $400 million for unpaid bodily injury losses at 31 December 2026, $55.4 million more than the $344.6 million finance has booked.
answer_source: task127/generator/figures.json (call, carried_musd, booked_musd, gap_musd, indicated_musd), asserted in task127/generator/checks.py, recomputed by task127/generator/verify.py

spine.entity: one loss payment, void or reissue on a bodily injury claimant feature in the legacy claims system

world.geography: United States (Iowa, Nebraska and South Dakota)

driver: The decisive quantity is a forward total projected from a history of cumulative progress by age in which the units carrying most of the amount began resolving more slowly partway through the record; the share of the amount settled tracks the share of units resolved rather than age, so the history has to be restated at the resolution shares the latest observations show before its age-to-age ratios are carried forward, and carrying them unrestated, or taking them from the latest periods alone, understates the total.
driver_concrete: Motor bodily injury unpaid at 31 December 2026 is projected from a quarterly paid triangle in which represented claims have settled at three quarters of their former pace since the claims platform went live in July 2024; paid development tracks the share of claimant features closed, so the triangle's history is restated at the latest diagonal's closed shares (Berquist and Sherman) before volume-weighted factors are taken, giving $399.8 million and a carried $400 million against the $344.6 million booked, where the unrestated paid chain ladder gives $316.8 million and a release.
stump: A competent solver stitches both claims systems' payments into a quarterly paid triangle, develops it with volume-weighted factors over all accident quarters to $316.8 million and would carry $325 million, a $19.6 million release against the $344.6 million booked; the step that lands it there is carrying the history's development factors onto accident quarters whose represented claims have settled more slowly since the July 2024 platform cutover, and only restating the history at the latest diagonal's closed shares gives $399.8 million and a carried $400 million, a strengthening of $55.4 million.
analyst_test: An analyst who reads every field and rule correctly stitches the two systems' payments into a quarterly paid triangle, develops it with volume-weighted factors over all accident quarters (the latest diagonals' factors land lower still) and would carry $325 million, a $19.6 million release against the $344.6 million booked; the triangle and every filed rule are right, and the figure is wrong because the factors carry the pre-cutover settlement pace onto quarters that are settling more slowly (executed on the clean truth in checks.py).
domain_test: Unpaid loss from a development triangle is the reserving actuary's core estimate, and restating paid development at the current disposal rate (Berquist and Sherman) is the field's own response when claims settle at a changed speed; with a utility's or a hospital's nouns there is no claim that closes, no closure ratio to restate paid development at and no booked reserve to strengthen, and the task stops reading the same.

differentiation.task46: task46's forward burden comes from a failure rate stationary in cumulative service exposure rebuilt per unit from a movement log; here nothing fails: a whole triangle's history is re-clocked at the share of claims closed, restated at the latest diagonal's closure ratios after a slowdown inside the record
differentiation.task127: v1 queued rebate slots behind a crew's meter-set capacity and v2 valued discharge packages by the care wait's excess over a concurrent equipment wait; here the decisive move is the field's settlement-rate restatement of paid development
differentiation.task138: task138 starts each unit's forward drawdown from the store the unit actually holds, rebuilt from its own last replenishment; here no unit's state is rebuilt: the whole history's age-to-age development is restated at the closure ratios the latest diagonal shows, because settlement slowed partway through the record
differentiation.task446: task446 backs a moved base rate out of a screen's flag share through error rates that carry across years; here nothing is screened and no base rate moves: the amount's development is re-clocked from age to the share of claims closed
differentiation.task125: task125 separates a fieldwork artifact in a rotating panel whose filtered intakes carry a difference for a fixed run; here no intake is filtered and no panel rotates: a claims history's paid development is restated at the share of claims closed after a settlement slowdown

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many of the period's placeable units a fixed team can finish before the period closes, because each unit counts only once that team performs one last step for it, the team's spare weekly capacity is visible only as the ceiling it held through an earlier unrelated surge, and the decision's own volume, bunched by its filed calendar into weeks no closed period approached, queues the later units past the close; the closed record's lag and an annual capacity check both pass, so the placeable count overstates the in-period total wherever the team is small and the units are many.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the part of each unit's recorded wait that the offered intervention removes, because the recorded wait fuses the step the intervention replaces with a concurrent step it leaves in place, so only the replaced step's excess over the concurrent one, built by joining separate operational logs, counts; ranking units by the recorded wait, or by the replaced step measured from the same start, credits the units whose concurrent step is slowest.

extracts run in January 2027, after the valuation date, so the register's status fields stand at the run date
voided and reissued checks in both payment ledgers
the general ledger booking the platform's nightly feed by posting date on Central time
features opened in error and closed as duplicates on the platform
